The eleven ratings for Xvivo

Xvivo Perfusion (XVIVO-SE): investment memo

Xvivo Perfusion: a strengthening business on an earnings base 37 percent below consensus, where the estimate cuts come before the evidence that re-rates the shares

Written 25 October 2026, three days after the Q3 2026 report. Share price SEK 223.4 (22 October 2026); market capitalisation about SEK 7.1 billion; enterprise value about SEK 6.85 billion. All money figures are in SEK millions unless stated. Sources, definitions, model notes and a glossary of acronyms are in the end-notes.

Summary of key insights, implications and conclusions

The case in three sentences.

  1. Xvivo is a strengthening business whose shares look cheap only on consensus earnings, and Viewforth's FY2027 EPS of 3.82 is 37 percent below consensus at 6.08.
  2. The next six to twelve months bring a cycle of estimate cuts and a likely re-dating of the company's 2027 targets, while the evidence that re-rates the shares (CE-marked heart quarters, reimbursement decisions and the FDA's posture) arrives after the cuts.
  3. The return to March 2028 is about +90 percent at Viewforth's central multiple of 45x and +130 percent at the guideline multiple of 53.9x, against a fair trough 37 to 50 percent below the price and a one-in-four chance of a loss, so the skew is favourable and improves with each estimate cut.

The business. Xvivo Perfusion, based in Gothenburg, makes the machines and fluids that keep donor organs viable between donor and recipient. The company has four parts:

  • Lung, the deep franchise. Perfadex Plus holds about 90 percent of static lung preservation, with patent cover to 2035, and STEEN Solution with the XPS machine is the only established platform for warm lung perfusion.
  • Heart, the large product entry in progress. Heart Assist Transport received its CE mark on 11 August 2026, and the FDA received its premarket approval (PMA) application on 28 September 2026. The heart system has the best clinical data in its category and costs about a third of the incumbent's price.
  • Abdominal, a contested European franchise. Liver Assist holds over half of European liver perfusion, but cheaper rivals contest it; kidney is an entrant.
  • United States services, a loss-maker. The organ-recovery services unit has lost money for six quarters.

Revenue is about 990 this year, at a 70 percent gross margin (company basis) and a 20 percent EBITDA margin. Xvivo has net cash of about 193, no debt leverage and no dividend. Demand is pulled by forces outside the company's control, and those forces are strengthening: donors after circulatory death are now half of United States donors and grow over 7 percent a year; a federal court upheld the United States rule that ranks organ procurement organisations on 28 September 2026; and hospital staffing shortages push organ evaluation into centralised hubs. Every competitor is growing 37 to 65 percent.

The seven conclusions that matter.

  1. 1Predictability

    Xvivo's business is predictable, but its shares are not. FY2027 revenue can be forecast to within about plus or minus 6 percent and the FY2027 EBITDA margin to within plus or minus 3 points. FY2027 EPS cannot be forecast to better than plus or minus 45 percent (a range of 2.1 to 5.6 around 3.8), because three items sit between EBITDA and EPS: about 120 of depreciation and amortisation, an unhedged krona and a tax rate that is normalising. The share price trades on EPS and on binary regulatory news, and it moves on company-specific news: 91 percent of the share price's variance over the last six months is idiosyncratic.

  2. 2Valuation

    The shares are cheap on the market's earnings and mid-range on Viewforth's earnings, and both readings cannot be true. The dashboard's valuation grade of A, and its reading of the 1st percentile of ten years, rest on consensus EPS of 6.08 for FY2027 and 9.47 for FY2028. Viewforth's model has 3.82 and 6.07, which are 37 and 36 percent lower. The gap arises because the sell-side's margin story stops at EBITDA: the brokers' numbers do not yet carry the disclosed CE-mark amortisation of 39 a year, a 20 percent tax rate or the end of 2026's currency gains. On Viewforth's EPS the shares trade at 39.9x 24-month-forward earnings, roughly the 25th to 40th percentile of the stock's own ten-year range and well above its floor. The case is therefore not "a cheap stock awaiting upgrades". The case is "the right business on the wrong earnings base, where the multiple must re-rate on lower numbers". That is a harder case to make, and this memo is built around it.

  1. 3Next 6 to 12 months

    Over the next six to twelve months, Xvivo faces a downgrade cycle that the stock has not yet completed. FY2027 consensus EPS (5.81 on the post-Q3 FactSet mean) should fall by 25 to 35 percent across four successive reports. The company's 2027 targets (an EBITDA margin above 30 percent and an EBIT margin above 20 percent) will be missed by a wide margin, and they are more likely than not to be re-dated at or soon after the Q4 report on 28 January 2027. Reported EPS will be flat in FY2027 against FY2026 (3.8 against 3.9), because 2026's one-off gains (a 16 percent tax rate and about 27 of currency and other financial income) give way to a full year of amortisation and a normal tax charge. The sell-side describes every one of these dynamics in words, but two of the four brokers have not put them into their numbers, and retail investors have priced in none of them. Sell-side momentum is graded F, and revisions are negative at every horizon.

  2. 4Beyond 12 months

    Beyond twelve months the skew turns favourable, for three reasons that the market under-weights. (a) Cash. The business already funds itself: operating cash flow was 182 in the first nine months of 2026, and free cash flow after all investment is about -3 this year and +15 next year on Viewforth's corrected inputs, against DNB Carnegie's -97 and -80. On the model's cash flows, net cash rises from about 190 to about 500 by end-2029 and over 800 by end-2030, so Xvivo could absorb a one-year FDA delay without raising equity. (b) A conservative FDA date. Viewforth assumes United States heart approval in late 2028 and launch in Q1 2029, which sits at about the 60th to 65th percentile of the plausible outcomes. The largest single estimate risk to Viewforth's forecasts is therefore skewed upward: approval in H1 2028 would add about 1.2 to 1.5 to FY2028 EPS. (c) The strategic floor. Terumo paid about 20x sales for OrganOx and Getinge paid 11x sales for Paragonix, whereas Xvivo's enterprise value is about 6.9x FY2026 sales. Xvivo's lung franchise alone, with 580 of revenue this year at gross margins above 80 percent, would be worth most of Xvivo's enterprise value at the lower of those two multiples.

  3. 5The FDA

    The same FDA decision is an upside risk to Viewforth's numbers and a downside risk to the share price. Consensus FY2028 EPS (9.47, and rising toward about 10.5 as RedEye adds United States heart revenue to 2028) assumes a United States heart launch in late 2027 or early 2028. However, 92 percent of the 2026 PMA cohort received a major-deficiency letter, and an advisory panel adds about 320 days to a review. If the FDA behaves as these base rates suggest, consensus FY2028 EPS falls 30 to 40 percent in one or two steps in H2 2027, while Viewforth's FY2028 EPS is unchanged or rises. The market trades on consensus, so 2027 carries a downside for the shares, driven by the FDA's timetable, that Viewforth's forecasts do not carry.

  4. 6Margins

    The margin expansion is real but late, and it reaches EBIT a year after it reaches EBITDA. Viewforth models the EBITDA margin rising from 20 percent in FY2026 to 24, 27, 29.5 and 31.5 percent in FY2027 to FY2030. That path is one to four points below consensus every year, because management keeps investing through three launches, and it means the company's "2027" margin targets are a 2029 to 2030 outcome. Between EBITDA and EPS, about 390 of capitalised regulatory assets (the CE mark, the PMA and the 510(k) clearance) amortise over ten years. As a result, a 14 percent EBITDA shortfall against FY2027 consensus becomes a 26 percent EBIT shortfall and a 37 percent EPS shortfall. Any upside scenario passes through the same compounding: 20 of extra EBITDA adds only about 0.5 to EPS.

  5. 7Return

    The total return at the guideline fair multiple is large (+130 percent to March 2028 and +241 percent to September 2029), and most of that return comes from earnings rather than from the multiple. On the model's 24-month-forward EPS, the earnings leg contributes +70 percent to March 2028 and +152 percent to September 2029, and the multiple leg contributes +35 percent in both cases (from 39.9x to the guideline 53.94x). The earnings leg already sits below consensus, so it is not stretched. The multiple leg requires the market to pay a 2024-type multiple on an earnings base 35 to 40 percent below today's consensus, and the market will pay that multiple only after consensus has reset and the European heart quarters and the FDA's posture are visible. My own central multiple for the 18-month horizon is 45x (the stock's "conservative" 35th-percentile band), below the guideline, and 45x still gives a return of about +90 percent. The downside case is a fair trough of 20 to 25x Viewforth's EPS, a share price of 110 to 140, which is 37 to 50 percent below today's price.

The implication for the decision: the setup improves with each estimate cut. Fundamental outcomes are skewed to the positive over two to three years, while the probability of guidance and sell-side upgrades is skewed to the negative over the next two to three reports. Each cut therefore improves the setup in three ways: the market's FY2027 EPS converges on Viewforth's, the company's targets are reset to levels the company can beat, and the evidence that re-rates the stock arrives after the cuts. That evidence is the CE-marked heart quarters from Q1 2027, Tier 2 reimbursement decisions, the liver 510(k) submission and the FDA's posture by mid-2027. The three quarters from Q4 2026 to Q2 2027 decide the European heart leg of the case; the twelve months after them decide the United States leg. Position sizing should assume that a drawdown of a third is ordinary for this stock.
